title: Fraud Features: TiDB as the System of Record Behind a Feature Platform
tagline: Chalk resolvers read fresh TiDB aggregates for online fraud features, checked live against direct SQL.
pattern: fintech ML platform team asking where TiDB fits versus a real-time feature platform (Chalk) and versus a key-value metric store.

metrics.label: Chalk online query p50
metrics.howMeasured: lab_runner.timed() wraps every ChalkClient.query call issued in the tick; samples are drained through lab_runner.summarize() once per 1000ms tick and the p50 field is emitted.

metrics.label: Chalk online query p99
metrics.howMeasured: Same sample window as chalk-query-p50; the p99 field of summarize() is emitted.

metrics.label: Direct-SQL baseline p99
metrics.howMeasured: lab_runner.timed() wraps the runner's own direct SQL query built by build_baseline_query and executed over the pooled TiDB connection; p99 of summarize() over the tick's samples is emitted.

metrics.label: Write-to-feature freshness lag
metrics.howMeasured: freshness_lag_ms(write_ts_ms, observed_ts_ms) is computed between a transaction's commit-return timestamp and the first cache-busted (staleness=0s) Chalk query whose txn_count_1h reflects it, polled every 100ms.

metrics.label: TiDB write rate
metrics.howMeasured: Count of transaction INSERT rows committed since the previous tick, divided by the 1.0s tick interval.

metrics.label: Chalk cache hit rate
metrics.howMeasured: Fraction of the tick's ChalkClient.query(include_meta=True) calls whose response meta indicates the value was served from the online store rather than a fresh resolver run; exact response field name confirmed in Task 11 before this metric is wired up (see Section 4).

metrics.label: Fraud flag flip latency
metrics.howMeasured: Seconds between the velocity-burst control event timestamp and the tick at which the Chalk-served velocity_flag for the burst user first reads true, from the fraud-flip check's polling loop.

phases.label: Seed data
phases.narration: We start with a normal book of transactions in TiDB - this is the system of record, nothing Chalk-specific about it yet.

phases.label: Steady state
phases.narration: Chalk is answering feature queries here by running SQL resolvers against TiDB. We're also running the exact same SQL ourselves, live, so you can see the two agree.

phases.label: Velocity burst
phases.narration: Watch one user's card get used sixty times in ninety seconds. That's TiDB taking the write load, and Chalk's feature flipping the moment the SQL resolver sees it.

phases.label: Staleness knob
phases.narration: This is the caching knob that's entirely Chalk's job, not TiDB's. Loosen it and queries get cheaper and staler; tighten it and every query re-runs the SQL resolver against TiDB.

phases.label: Wrap-up
phases.narration: TiDB was the source of truth and the aggregate engine the whole time. Chalk gave us naming, caching, and a serving API on top of it.

checks.label: Chalk feature equals direct-SQL baseline
checks.description: The Chalk-served txn_count_1h, amount_sum_24h, and distinct_merchants_24h for the sampled user match the runner's own direct SQL query against TiDB for the same user and timestamp.

checks.label: Velocity flag flips within the burst
checks.description: The Chalk-served velocity_flag for the burst user reads true within 30 seconds of the velocity-burst control firing.

controls.label: Fire velocity burst
controls.description: Inserts 60 transactions for one designated burst user over about 90 seconds, then polls until velocity_flag flips true or 30s elapses.

controls.label: Toggle staleness (cached / fresh)
controls.description: Flips Chalk queries between the feature-level default max_staleness and an explicit 0s override on every output feature.

controls.label: Burst write rate
controls.description: Raises the transaction generator's write rate tenfold across many users for 20 seconds.
